latest_attempt.failure: The corrected scheduler config reported has_mamba_layers=true and needs_kv_cache_zeroing=true, service/graph/API readiness passed, all 192 native all-head bindings passed, and the prefix-hit delta was 4608. Nevertheless, the short response was not exact and three identical long-prefix replays diverged. The config marker did not prove that aligned split, zeroing, or Mamba copy branches actually executed, so scheduler-awareness alone is rejected and the next canary adds branch-local evidence without changing behavior.

Treat v12r18 as a completed failed numerical experiment: lifecycle configuration flags were restored, but exact output and deterministic prefix replay still failed. Do not rerun the same bytes/root and do not benchmark or run E2E quality.

Use v12r19 only as a branch-evidence control. It must prove the scheduler aligned-split branch, the scheduler zeroing branch, and the heterogeneous Mamba copy branch with bounded runtime events while retaining the all-head geometry and unchanged outputs.

Before v12r19, commit/push the prepared observability-only plugin, verify the immutable root branch-evidence-all-heads-v12r19 is absent, and repeat the live PID/HBM/container/port/image/lock audit. One NPU run only; never reuse the v12r18 root.

Do not tune DASC retention, benchmark performance, or run E2E quality while the all-head control is nondeterministic.

Instrument the first cache-hit token boundary: capture request identity, local block mapping, compact source row, dense active-slot row, and state checksums before restore, before native recurrent execution, and after checkpoint.

Add a plugin-disabled dense lifecycle control and an all-head bridge control under the same long-prefix request sequence; require exact first-token logits or token IDs and stable state evolution before restoring pruning.

Treat v12r13 as the exact dense control: prompt_tokens=1938, identical_replays=true, all outputs VERIFIED, prefix_cache_hit_delta=3072, artifact SHA256 715aba4ddf6b9f35259034c96ea17051d66d350f20c71be83c54df48d20ce2d8.

Treat v12r14 and v12r15 as control-plane failures only: v12r14 exposed aligned mixed-group admission, and v12r15 copied an obsolete canary that did not accept the diagnostic gate. Neither is numerical evidence.

Treat v12r16 and v12r17 as decision-changing numerical evidence: all-head bridge and bridge-bypassed native-cache controls both remained unstable, so the bridge is not the sole cause. The next bounded hypothesis is mixed aggregate lifecycle awareness, not more bridge instrumentation.
Keep the verified dense-storage numerical canary as a closed reachability result; do not tune or benchmark it as a performance candidate.
Keep the immutable v12r4 root as a failed graph-capture result: real DASC activation passed, but the first-spec order was not instrumented and must not be inferred from model order.

Keep commit 373b448 and immutable v12r5 artifacts as the rejected first-spec dispatch attempt; the adapter fired on four ranks but storage_first and dispatch_first were already the same attention layer and graph capture failed identically.
Keep the failed adapter out of the active plugin tree while preserving its Git history.

Complete the paper-to-code parity matrix and label the current implementation paper-derived DASC-NR Ascend adaptation until an author repository is released or the missing SGLang mechanisms are independently reproduced.
Treat v12r6 as superseded: restoring compact state before every model forward violates the paper's cache-load boundary by erasing omitted-head updates accumulated after the first token.

Keep the integrated request-owned dense active-state bridge: a request keeps one stable dense slot across decode steps and physical block transitions; compact restore occurs only on true new/resumed prefix Load.

Keep the request-lifecycle regression gate: first Load zero-fills omitted heads, a normal step updates them, same-request block transition preserves them, and release/reactivate zero-fills them again while restoring retained heads.

Treat the TP4 MAX-padding tax as measured, not hypothetical: W_max=64 retains 1728 raw heads but stores 2084 after contiguous layerwise rank equalization. The exact whole-GQA-group TP4 bound is 1828; 1788 is only the arbitrary-per-head lower bound. If v12r7 is correct but weak, compare coupled group permutation against paper-equivalent variable-split Store/Load rather than tuning around the 1.11x temporal ceiling.

Use the operator-authorized DASC-local idle-claim override only when NPU4-7 have no device-side process and idle HBM. Record vllm_main_au, vllm_26_au and vllm_23_au declarations, never stop them, and fail closed if any real process or HBM allocation appears before launch.

Do not launch v12r6; its controller now fails closed on the semantic supersession. Prepare a newly named immutable attempt only after request identity, release/resume, metadata remapping, and graph-pointer gates pass.
Do not start formal performance or quality work unless a materially different successor passes service, strict canary, activation, ownership, and physical-byte verification.
Use commit 5f93b14 cache-hit quality adapter for formal quality runs; --require-cache-hit must fail closed on a zero hit delta.
Use the hash-pinned tokenizer context audit and max_model_len=44032 for both formal arms; reject truncation and the preserved invalid two-token audit.
Only after a materially different successor passes the physical mechanism gate, run the one-switch cache-hit TTFT and input-throughput benchmark.
